coverage_summary: The reconstruction captures many explicitly stated modality boundaries and appropriately leaves several opaque modules unresolved. Revision is required because documented preprocessing chains, conditional branches, contrastive training, sequence inputs, evaluation post-processing, and some operation order/port bindings are missing or unsupported.

findings.detail: The preprocessing step collapses explicitly documented ordered transformations into one opaque boundary. It omits library-size normalization, log transformation, gene-symbol mapping, vocabulary filtering, fixed-dimensional conversion, structured evidence extraction, GPT-4 verbalization, and quality filtering.

evidence.quote: For count-based spatial transcriptomics data, raw counts were normalized for library size, logtransformed and mapped to a common gene-symbol vocabulary whenever possible.
These structured fields were inserted into an evidence-constrained prompt and verbalized into concise biological descriptions using GPT-4
Generated descriptions were filtered for missing required evidence fields, malformed gene symbols, unsupported tissue names, formatting failures and obvious violations of the evidence constraints.

findings.required_change: Preserve the documented order with separate normalize and log_transform calls, explicit mapping/filtering and fixed-dimensional conversion, plus an opaque boundary for ssGSEA/evidence extraction and GPT-4 verbalization followed by quality selection.

findings.detail: The fixed-dimensional gene-encoder input is an orphan node. The reconstruction creates stage_ii_gene_encoder_input but supplies no operation or edge from the expression profile/preprocessing path.

evidence.quote: The processed expression vector was converted into the fixed-dimensional representation expected by the gene encoder.
where the gene encoder first maps the gene expression profile into molecular embeddings

findings.required_change: Add the documented conversion from the processed expression vector to stage_ii_gene_encoder_input and connect it to the gene encoder.

findings.detail: The Stage III gene path feeds spot_gene_counts directly into an opaque encoder/Q-Former/projector boundary, omitting the documented preprocessing required before model input. The representation name “gene_expression_counts” is also not established for this trajectory.

evidence.quote: Gene expression matrices were processed separately for each dataset before being used as model input.
The processed expression vector was converted into the fixed-dimensional representation expected by the gene encoder.
Each local image patch and matched gene expression vector were paired with a transcriptome-grounded description derived from the same spot.

findings.required_change: Add the applicable conditional preprocessing path before the gene encoder, and label the input as a gene expression vector unless raw-count status is explicitly supported.

findings.detail: The Stage III gene path combines three documented ordered components into one null boundary, despite the paper specifying gene encoder → Q-Former → projector and the 32-token output.

evidence.quote: the gene encoder first maps the gene expression profile into molecular embeddings, the Q-Former compresses the molecular representation into 32 query virtual tokens, and the projector maps these virtual tokens into the language-model hidden space.

findings.required_change: Decompose the path into gene encoding, Q-Former compression, and projection, using intermediate nodes and preserving the documented order; leave each internal computation opaque where necessary.

findings.detail: The Stage III visual path similarly collapses the documented visual feature and resampler stages and does not preserve the reported fixed output of 64 visual virtual tokens.

evidence.quote: Visual features are converted into a fixed number of vision virtual tokens through a visual encoder and a resampler module.
histology-derived visual features are compressed into 64 visual virtual tokens

findings.required_change: Represent visual encoding and resampling as ordered opaque stages with an intermediate visual-feature node, and retain 64 as the documented output cardinality.

findings.detail: Stage III sequence assembly binds raw tri_modal_visual_virtual_tokens to the sequence boundary even though the paper states that modality tokens are projected into language-model space before insertion into the unified sequence.

evidence.quote: The resulting visual and molecular token spans replace reserved modality placeholders in the input sequence
projected into the same token space as the molecular virtual tokens.

findings.required_change: Bind tri_modal_projected_visual_tokens, not tri_modal_visual_virtual_tokens, to the multimodal sequence assembly boundary.

findings.detail: The Stage III assembly does not preserve the explicitly documented image-only, gene-only, and joint image-gene branches. It passes both modality operands as if they were always simultaneously present.

evidence.quote: During this stage, the model was trained on image-only, gene-only and joint imagegene input formats to support flexible downstream use.
General-domain image-text and instructionfollowing samples were mixed at a low proportion to preserve general multimodal and language-following competence.

findings.required_change: Represent image-only, gene-only, joint, and retained general-domain branches explicitly, with conditional modality bypasses and separate branch-specific sequence inputs.

findings.detail: The documented multimodal contrastive alignment objective is absent from the Stage III trajectory. The reconstruction includes sequence assembly but no boundary for image-text, gene-text, and image-gene InfoNCE alignment using projected token spans.

evidence.quote: The main alignment objective combined autoregressive generation with multimodal contrastive alignment
Pairwise InfoNCE-style losses were computed across available modality pairs, including image-text, gene-text and image-gene pairs when present
Modality-level representations were obtained from the corresponding projected token spans before contrastive comparison.

findings.required_change: Add an opaque contrastive-alignment objective boundary with the three conditional modality-pair branches and projected-token-span inputs; retain unspecified pooling, negatives, temperature, and loss details as uncertainty.

findings.detail: Stage I creates text_embeddings and uses it as an input to sequence assembly, but no text-token embedding lookup or opaque producer connects text_tokens to text_embeddings.

evidence.quote: The virtual tokens are then projected into the hidden dimension of the language model and inserted into placeholders, thereby forming a unified input embedding sequence.
The final multimodal sequence consists of text tokens, optional visual virtual tokens and optional gene virtual tokens

findings.required_change: Add an explicit text-token-to-language-embedding lookup boundary with an unspecified embedding table, or remove the orphan text_embeddings node and represent this conversion inside the opaque sequence-construction boundary.

findings.detail: The frozen regression trajectory omits the documented training-only selection of the top 50 target genes and the section-level 10-fold split context.

evidence.quote: we used section-level 10-fold crossvalidation.
The prediction targets were the top 50 genes with the highest expression in the training set

findings.required_change: Add the training-split section partition and target-gene ranking/selection context before the regression-head output, without treating the selected panel as a model input tensor.

findings.detail: The fine-tuned regression trajectory also omits the documented training-split top-50 target selection and does not preserve the exact trainable-layer condition in the embedding extraction invocation.

evidence.quote: The prediction targets were the top 50 genes with the highest expression in the training set
the regression head and the last six layers of the visual encoder were trainable.

findings.required_change: Record the training-split target-gene selection and set the fine-tuned visual extraction state to the last six visual-encoder layers trainable, with the remaining visual encoder frozen as documented.

findings.detail: The embedding-based spatial-domain trajectory does not preserve the three conditional input branches. Its single extraction step receives both image and gene inputs despite the paper evaluating image-only, gene-only, and joint embeddings.

evidence.quote: frozen model embeddings were extracted from image-only, gene-only or joint image-gene input

findings.required_change: Add explicit image-only, gene-only, and joint branches or conditional bypasses before the classification head.

findings.detail: The generative spatial-domain trajectory likewise collapses image-only, gene-only, and joint input formats into one unconditional assembly step.

evidence.quote: For generative evaluation, the model received image-only, gene-only or joint image-gene input and generated a structured biological response.

findings.required_change: Represent the three input branches and their branch-specific modality availability before generation; retain the fusion implementation as unresolved.

findings.detail: The zero-shot post-processing boundary omits several rules that are explicitly documented: lowercasing, punctuation removal, normalized-label/alias matching, exact-one-label assignment, and treating ambiguous responses as incorrect.

evidence.quote: Generated responses were converted to lowercase, punctuation was removed and the resulting text was matched against normalized candidate labels and predefined label aliases.
Responses that could not be mapped unambiguously to a single candidate label were treated as incorrect.

findings.required_change: Preserve these parser operations and the ambiguity branch as invocation parameters or an explicitly described opaque parser boundary.

findings.detail: The PathVQA trajectory stops at answer generation and omits the documented open-ended/closed-ended evaluation branches, yes/no normalization, answer normalization, and multiset token-level recall matching.

evidence.quote: Evaluation followed the standard separation between open-ended and closed-ended questions.
Closedended questions were scored after normalizing yes/no outputs.
For open-ended questions, both predictions and reference answers were normalized.
Performance was reported as token-level recall, defined as the fraction of reference tokens appearing in the prediction, with multiset matching.

findings.required_change: Add the open-ended and closed-ended answer-processing branches and the documented benchmark matching operation after generation.

findings.detail: The whole-slide trajectory invents a separate tumour-region selection operation after low-magnification review. The paper documents identification of regions followed directly by high-magnification patch selection from those regions.

evidence.quote: Each slide was first reviewed at low magnification to identify tumour-rich regions and representative tumour-stroma interfaces.
High-magnification patches were then selected from these regions for local morphological assessment.

findings.required_change: Remove the unsupported candidate-region-to-selected-region selection step, or retain it only as an explicitly unresolved part of low-magnification region identification; connect identified regions directly to high-magnification patch selection.
